title: Can green technologies deliver energy security in an unstable world?
summary:
Use of global primary energy — naturally occurring energy sources that have not undergone any processing by humans — more than doubled between 1980 and 2025.
Although the share of primary energy generated by renewables is growing, oil, coal and gas still account for about 80% of energy production.
Source: Our World in DataThe IEA defines energy security as reliable, affordable access to all fuels and energy sources.
The IEA says that this could drop to $50 by 2035 and that geothermal energy could generate 8% of global electricity supplies by 2050.
Efforts to develop more efficient solar cells could also help countries to improve their energy security by increasing sustainable domestic electricity supplies.

title: Thick smog shrouds New Delhi after Diwali firecrackers add to seasonal pollution
summary:
Thick smog shrouds New Delhi after Diwali firecrackers add to seasonal pollutiontoggle caption i Manish Swarup/APNEW DELHI — A thick blanket of smog shrouded India's capital Monday after firecrackers lit up the skies over New Delhi during Diwali celebrations, compounding dangerously high pollution levels and intensifying the seasonal air pollution crisis that grips the city every year.
Sponsor MessageIndia's Supreme Court in October had sought to limit Diwali pollution by restricting conventional firecrackers and allowing only approved "green firecrackers" under specified conditions for three-hour windows on Saturday and Sunday.
Isyad, a New Delhi resident who uses one name, said the worsening smog was taking a toll on his health.
Pollution worsens as Diwali fireworks coincide with cooler weather and smoke from crop-residue fires in neighboring states of Punjab and Haryana.
The smoke drifts toward New Delhi, adding to pollution from vehicles, industries, construction dust and other local sources.

title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week
summary:
The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups.
But the speed of the transition to electric has been hotly debated, including within the cabinet.
Asked about reports the targets would be reduced, Burnham dismissed this as "speculation", adding: "No decision has been made at this point."
The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders welcomed the government's review of the EV targets when it was announced in the summer.

title: The superpower battle over energy, and the impact on your bills
summary:
Since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, oil and gas prices have soared.
And there's a bigger threat looming over all of this: the warming climate.
But keeping bills down while cutting emissions is proving hard – and not just for the UK.
Energy and climate policy has become the front line in a contest between the world's two energy superpowers, leaving everyone else squeezed in between.
America is betting on fossil-fuel molecules: pumping record volumes of oil and gas and pressing its allies to buy them.

title: Daily briefing: The ‘overshoot COP’ kicks off
summary:
The COP31 climate conference begins, with ‘climate overshoot’ a key talking point.
Plus, the surprising benefits of ‘pink noise’ and the role of AI chatbots to support men’s mental health.
(Maximilien Lamy/AFP via Getty)COP climate summit faces overshoot of 1.5 °C A troubling reality hangs over the United Nations climate conference (COP31) opening in Turkey today: overshoot.
Researchers analysed 1,000 conversations between strangers and found that participants felt a stronger sense of connection with their partner when their chats had featured more pink noise.
A separate research team found that pink noise can also help to kickstart the brain’s ‘wash cycle’ during sleep.

title: Oil prices are so high that CO2 emissions from fossil fuels are dropping
summary:
Between 2019 and 2025, carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels grew by about 0.8 percent annually, according to a new study published in Nature Climate Change.
But 2026 is set to buck that trend: high oil prices, as well as the continued rise of green technology—solar power, wind and electric cars—will cause a “short-term” 0.4 percent drop, according to the study.
“However, in both cases, emissions rebounded the year after,” Le Quéré says.
If oil prices return to their prewar levels, Le Quéré and her colleagues expect to see emissions rise once more.
“We show that to tackle climate change and guarantee that global fossil emissions decrease durably, the expansion of renewable energy and electric vehicles need to accelerate further,” Le Quéré says.

title: US Senate advances major bill boosting energy infrastructure
summary:
Rare bipartisan bill requires data centres to pay for infrastructure, but environmental groups say it falls short.
The United States Senate has voted to move forward on a bipartisan bill that would speed up the process to build new data centres and energy infrastructure in the country.
“This Bill is a BIG WIN for U.S. ENERGY INDEPENDENCE and DOMINANCE”, Trump posted on social media Monday as he encouraged lawmakers to support it.
It would also force owners of energy-hungry data centres to pay for the infrastructure that is needed to power them.
AdvertisementBut despite the bill’s claims of increasing clean energy projects, environmental organisations are opposed to the legislation.

title: Biotech innovations are an opportunity to limit climate change
summary:
Progress in each case, whether preventing dangerous climate change or stemming biodiversity loss, is too slow.
Now, the field offers strategies for protecting both climate and biodiversity from the many damaging effects of industrial agriculture.
Land clearance and land-use change contributes up to five billion tonnes of carbon annually — and is a major cause of biodiversity loss.
Advances in biotechnology that limit land use should be deployed to slow down the rise in global temperatures and biodiversity loss.
High-yielding crops produced using industrial agriculture have helped to feed the world but have also had a devastating effect on biodiversity.

title: The Gloucestershire swan sanctuary fighting climate change
summary:
Most people know rainforests are vital in the fight against climate change, but now scientists say wetlands could be even more important.
Saltmarshes, mangrove swamps and wetlands can absorb carbon "four times faster than trees", according to the charity the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust (WWT).
Celebrating 80 years since WWT's first wetland bird reserve was founded at Slimbridge, in Gloucestershire, the charity's leaders have called for one million hectares of wetlands to be restored across the world.
Sarah Fowler, CEO of WWT, said: "They are mood-boosting, flood-buffering, water-purifying, incredible habitats.
But we have lost 85% of the world's wetlands."

title: Smog blankets New Delhi as Diwali firecrackers worsen air quality
summary:
Air quality in Indian capital reaches severe levels, posing heightened health risks for more than 30 million residents.
Share Smog blankets New Delhi as Diwali firecrackers worsen air quality on social mediaHeavy smog has blanketed New Delhi after firecrackers lit up the Indian capital during Diwali celebrations, worsening the seasonal pollution crisis.
Last month, India’s Supreme Court put in place restrictions to limit Diwali pollution, allowing only approved “green firecrackers” under specified conditions for three-hour windows on Saturday and Sunday.
Seasonal pollutionOn Wednesday, days before Diwali, toxic air pollution in New Delhi surged to more than 30 times the WHO’s recommended daily limit, data from air monitors showed.
AdvertisementVehicles account for 23 percent of New Delhi’s winter pollution, while biomass burning, including farm stubble fires, contributes 20 percent, according to India’s Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

summary:
